name: Nitrogen
description: Nitrogen is a primary constituent of amino acids, proteins, and chlorophyll in plant physiology.
importance: Drives rapid vegetative shoot growth, leaf canopy development, cellular photosynthesis, and overall biomass accumulation.
deficiency_symptoms: Generalized yellowing (chlorosis) initiating on older lower leaves, stunted plant height, spindly stems, and reduced tillering.
excess_symptoms: Excessively dark green foliage, delayed floral initiation and crop maturity, weak succulent stems susceptible to lodging, and higher vulnerability to fungal pathogens.
management_practices: Apply nitrogenous fertilizers in split doses (basal, tillering, panicle initiation) to avoid leaching.
Incorporate leguminous green manure crops (e.g., Sesbania, Sunn hemp) into crop rotations to fix atmospheric nitrogen.
Utilize neem-coated urea or slow-release formulations to increase nitrogen-use efficiency.
